bio:
Toronto singer-songwriter Lia Pappas-Kemps first reached a broad audience as an actor on Anne with an E, but her music has developed into a distinct creative identity built around intimate writing, guitar-led arrangements and a willingness to let songs unfold gradually. Early releases including the EP Gleam introduced a restrained alternative-folk sound and helped establish her as an emerging songwriter rather than an actor crossing casually into music. Songs such as "Jinx" and "Revolving Doors" drew attention for their emotional specificity and careful pacing, setting up a fuller debut era.

Her first full-length album, Winged, arrived in March 2026 through Coalition Music. Recorded in Toronto, the album expands the quieter textures of her earlier work with moments of distorted alternative rock, spacious production and more dynamic band arrangements. "Towers" became an early focal point, pairing a relationship-at-the-breaking-point lyric with a more forceful guitar sound, while the album as a whole showed a young songwriter moving beyond the scale of an introductory EP without losing the close-up quality of her writing.

Pappas-Kemps remains early in her recording career, which is important context for assessing her significance. She is not yet a legacy figure, but Winged places her within a strong Toronto lineage of singer-songwriters who blur folk intimacy, indie rock and literate pop writing. Her profile is worth following because the transition from Gleam to a confident debut album suggests an artist developing a durable songwriting voice rather than simply building momentum around a single breakout track.

Libby Ember is a Canadian indie-pop singer-songwriter based in Montreal whose intimate writing blends indie folk, dream pop and bedroom pop. A Concordia University music student, she emerged with the 2025 EP I Kill Spiders and has continued building an audience with emotionally direct songs about longing, anxiety and relationships.
Lightman Jarvis Ecstatic Band is the Canadian experimental duo of Toronto-born Romy Lightman and Montréal artist Yves Jarvis, blending psych-folk, neo-soul, dream pop and improvised indie rock.

British Columbia electronic-pop duo LIINKS pairs Georgia Murray's vocals and songwriting with producer Tony Day's beat-driven production. The pair met in Victoria and developed a sound that blends R&B, pop and electronic music, earning Canadian radio play and millions of streams.

Toronto-born Regent Park rapper Lil Berete is known for melodic street rap that helped bridge rival sides of his neighbourhood, building an international audience through singles such as Northside and Southside and the Icebreaker projects.

LIL Darklord is an alias of Toronto producer and artist Jahmar Carter, also known as Daxz. Carter emerged from Toronto's hip-hop production scene and has credits connected to Drake, KILLY, The Weeknd and other major artists. Slump City, his 2018 collaboration with WondaGurl from the Yesterday project, is the LIL Darklord credit in the Northern Dial library.
Toronto-born singer-songwriter Lilyisthatyou, born Lily Davies, is a Canadian pop artist whose irreverent, sex-positive music blends dance-pop, indie rock and hip-hop influence.

Limblifter began in Vancouver in the mid-1990s as a side project for The Age of Electric brothers Ryan and Kurt Dahle with bassist Ian Somers, but quickly developed an identity of its own. The self-titled debut produced Canadian alternative-radio staples including "Tinfoil," "Vicious" and "Screwed It Up," establishing Ryan Dahle's combination of crooked guitar textures, melodic power pop and idiosyncratic songwriting as the band's centre of gravity. When The Age of Electric ended, Limblifter became his primary long-term vehicle.

The 2000 album Bellaclava deepened that approach with songs such as "Ariel vs. Lotus" and "Wake Up to the Sun." Lineup changes became part of the band's history: Kurt Dahle and Todd Fancey moved into The New Pornographers, while Ryan rebuilt Limblifter around new collaborators for I/O in 2004. Across those changes, the group accumulated five Top 11 Canadian radio hits and three JUNO nominations, giving it a durable place in the country's alternative-rock network even without the scale of a conventional arena-rock career.

Limblifter's later catalogue has made that continuity clearer. Pacific Milk arrived in 2015 and Little Payne in 2022, while the band returned to regular live activity with a lineup centred on Ryan Dahle and bassist Megan Bradfield and, more recently, drummer Jeremy Taggart of Our Lady Peace. The group's longevity also mirrors Dahle's wider role as a producer, collaborator and member of Mounties. Limblifter matters as more than a 1990s radio memory: it is one of the connective projects linking The Age of Electric, The New Pornographers and several generations of Vancouver and Canadian indie rock.

Lincoln Blaché is a Juno-nominated Canadian recording artist, songwriter and producer from Mississauga. He first gained wider recognition through his featured vocal on Doman & Gooding's dance single Runnin', then continued into independent music and artist development as founder of MADE IN SAUGA. Runnin' is the Lincoln credit in the Northern Dial library.
Halifax singer Linda Carvery is an African Nova Scotian jazz and gospel vocalist whose career spans recording, theatre, community leadership and arts advocacy.

Lindo P, also known as Lindissimo, is a Canadian reggae and dancehall DJ, selector, recording artist and songwriter based in Toronto. Originally from St. Ann, Jamaica, he immigrated to Toronto with his family and became embedded in the city's Canadian-Caribbean music community through 416 Sound, solo releases and collaborations with artists including Kardinal Offishall and Shawn Desman.

LiquidLtd is a Montreal-linked music project associated with vocalist and founding member Stephen 'Liquid' Hawley. Hawley is based in Montreal, Quebec, and the project maintains an independent catalogue spanning releases and online performances. Northern Dial carries LiquidLtd as part of its Canadian independent music catalogue.

Liza is a Toronto-born Ethiopian-Canadian R&B and neo-soul singer-songwriter whose intimate, airy songwriting has earned national recognition, including a 2023 Black Canadian Music Award. Her catalogue includes February 29, DONE IS DONE and The Alternate Ending, alongside collaborations across Toronto's contemporary R&B scene. Five songs from The Alternate Ending era account for her Northern Dial library credits.

Toronto singer, songwriter and producer Yuri Koller, formerly known as Lokz and credited as Lokkz on JD Era's 2012 track "No Handouts," built his early catalogue through R&B and hip-hop collaborations before releasing music under his own name.

Lokz is the former stage name of Toronto singer, songwriter and producer Yuri Koller. Koller built his early career in Toronto under the Lokz name, appearing on JD Era's 'No Handouts,' performing at Toronto showcases and earning a slot at the first OVO Fest before later recording under his birth name. Northern Dial carries Lokz as part of its Toronto hip-hop and R&B catalogue.

LOONY is a Toronto singer and songwriter whose records sit between R&B, neo-soul and left-field pop. Her writing tends to stay close to the body: small details, tangled feelings and melodies that feel conversational instead of oversized. After the 2024 self-titled album LOONY and the 2026 project JUST HAPPY TO BE HERE!, she returned in July 2026 with the single RaGDOLL, keeping the focus on loose groove, vocal phrasing and emotional messiness rather than polished pop symmetry.

Toronto rapper Lord Juco is a Canadian underground hip-hop artist whose dense, sample-driven releases and collaborations connect him to the city's independent boom-bap scene and the wider Griselda orbit.
Manitoba-born singer, composer and producer Loreena McKennitt is a Canadian music icon whose self-produced catalogue blends Celtic, folk and world-music traditions.

loser supreme is a Montreal-based independent artist working in alternative pop and hip-hop-adjacent sounds. His SoundCloud profile identifies Montreal as his home base and documents a growing catalogue of self-released tracks. Northern Dial carries loser supreme as part of its contemporary Montreal independent music catalogue.

Lotus James is a Canadian hip-hop artist associated with the Lunch Room Poetz collective and the Greater Toronto underground scene. HipHopCanada featured Lotus James in the group's 'LRP Cypher,' describing the lineup as representing Canadian hip-hop, and he has continued to appear on Toronto-area releases through Motive Music Canada. Northern Dial carries Lotus James as part of its contemporary Canadian underground hip-hop catalogue.
Saint-Hubert, Québec rapper and producer Lou Phelps, born Louis-Philippe Celestin, makes groove-heavy hip-hop and is also known for collaborating with his brother Kaytranada in The Celestics.

Louis-Charles is a Quebec City quintet whose music blends post-punk, post-rock and alternative pop with francophone songwriting. The group released the EP BABY in 2023 and followed it with the album Louis-Charles II in 2026, establishing a growing presence in Quebec's independent rock scene. Northern Dial carries Louis-Charles as part of its contemporary francophone alternative catalogue.
Québec singer-songwriter, guitarist and producer Louis-Jean Cormier is a French-Canadian artist known for his solo catalogue and his work with the band Karkwa.

Louke Man is an earlier styling of Toronto producer and DJ Loukeman, born Luke Fenton. His catalogue under the name includes the Sd-1 era and other early releases that helped establish his lo-fi, sample-heavy approach before he consolidated the spelling as Loukeman.

Toronto-born and raised producer, multi-instrumentalist and DJ Loukeman, born Luke Fenton, makes sample-heavy electronic music that blurs house, R&B, indie and ambient textures. His Sd mixtape trilogy built a cult following before collaborations with artists including PinkPantheress, A$AP Rocky, Aminé and MIKE pushed his production into a wider international spotlight.
Nova Scotia-bred, Toronto-based singer-songwriter Loviet, born Natalie Lynn, is a Canadian indie-rock and alternative-pop artist whose sound pairs 1990s guitar grit with polished melodic hooks.
Orléans, Ontario-born singer Luce Dufault is a prominent francophone Canadian vocalist whose career spans pop recordings, major Québec stage productions and long-running live performance.

Luka Ferraro is a Filipino-Italian songwriter and producer based in Montreal whose music spans indie rock and pop. He first gained attention as one half of 20 Minutes Til Sunrise before expanding into solo releases and collaborations across Montreal's independent music community. Northern Dial carries Luka Ferraro as part of its contemporary Montreal indie catalogue.

Luminous is a hip-hop artist connected to Toronto's late-1990s underground scene through work with Canadian rapper and producer Frankenstein. Credits include scratches on Frankenstein's Toronto-recorded 'The Rain Is Gone' EP and the collaboration 'Oxygen.' Northern Dial carries Luminous as part of its classic Toronto underground hip-hop catalogue.
Mississauga singer-songwriter Luna Elle is a Ghanaian-Canadian R&B and soul artist known for a deep vocal tone, emotionally direct writing and multiple Juno Award nominations.

Toronto rapper Luu Breeze is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose mixtape-era catalogue helped document the city's mid-2000s independent rap scene through street-oriented lyricism and Southern-influenced production.
Halifax rapper LXVNDR is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose dark, mystical writing and imagery sit over underground rap production shaped by Nova Scotia's independent scene.
Lavaltrie-born, Montréal-based singer-songwriter Léonie Gray is a Québec soul and R&B artist whose music combines jazz-influenced vocals, bilingual songwriting and contemporary pop production.

LÖV is a Cree R&B and soul singer-songwriter from Treaty 6 Territory whose music is built around resilience, self-definition and matriarchal strength. Her work draws from UK-influenced soul and contemporary R&B, but the emotional centre is intensely personal: songs about independence, family, healing and the decision to reclaim control of her own story. That focus has made LÖV's rise feel less like a conventional debut campaign than a deliberate artistic reset, with each release strengthening a persona grounded in both vulnerability and authority.

A creative partnership with Montréal producer Connor Seidel helped sharpen that sound into a polished, spacious form where LÖV's smoky vocals remain the main event. Early singles including "Mama," "Matriarch," "Relate" and "Sister Era" built substantial streaming momentum, while "Mama" reached No. 1 on the Indigenous Music Countdown. Her music has also appeared on major Spotify and Apple Music editorial playlists, and coverage from CBC and APTN has helped expand her profile beyond western Canada.

By 2025 and 2026, LÖV's presence was extending beyond recordings into fashion, live performance and artist-development spaces, including Native Fashion Week and a Massey Hall artist-in-residence program. Her debut project Iskwêw gives that growth a clear frame: contemporary soul built around Indigenous womanhood, family and autonomy without treating any of those subjects as marketing categories. Within Northern Dial's Indigenous coverage, LÖV represents the R&B side of a broader movement in which Indigenous artists are defining modern pop and soul on their own terms.
Toronto-born singer-songwriter LØLØ is a Canadian pop-rock and pop-punk artist known for confessional lyrics, sharp hooks and an online audience that helped launch her international career.

maadlvc is a Toronto DJ and selector whose sets move through hip-hop, R&B, dance and club music. Their SoundCloud profile identifies Toronto as home and documents a catalogue of mixes and radio appearances. Northern Dial carries maadlvc as part of its contemporary Toronto DJ catalogue.

Raised in Edmonton, Mac DeMarco became one of the most recognizable Canadian figures in 2010s indie rock by making deliberately loose, home-recorded guitar music feel both eccentric and unusually intimate. After earlier work under the name Makeout Videotape, he established the Mac DeMarco catalogue with Rock and Roll Night Club and 2 in 2012. Songs such as "Ode to Viceroy" and "My Kind of Woman" paired warped guitar tones, dry humour and melodic soft-rock instincts with a recording style that made the seams of the process part of the appeal.

Salad Days in 2014 broadened that audience and became a Polaris Music Prize Short List nominee. The record refined his woozy guitar sound while allowing more anxiety and self-examination into the writing, and tracks including "Chamber of Reflection" became enduring entry points into his catalogue. Another One and This Old Dog moved further toward restrained songwriting, acoustic guitar and synthesizers, with This Old Dog in particular turning family history, aging and distance into some of his most direct work. Here Comes the Cowboy followed in 2019 before DeMarco increasingly stepped outside the conventional album cycle.

That independent streak became structural as well as aesthetic. He launched Mac's Record Label, issued the instrumental travelogue Five Easy Hot Dogs and then released the enormous 199-track One Wayne G collection in 2023. Guitar, released in 2025, returned to a concise song-based format and was written, recorded, produced and mixed by DeMarco himself at his Los Angeles home. Across those shifts, his significance lies in how thoroughly a self-recorded Canadian indie sensibility travelled internationally: his bent guitar tones, unhurried performances and deliberately personal production language became a widely recognizable vocabulary without requiring him to move toward conventional rock polish.

British Columbia rapper Madchild, born Shane Bunting, first became nationally known as one of the founding MCs of Swollen Members. His tightly wound, high-pitched delivery and battle-rap instincts were central to the Vancouver group's rise from the late-1990s underground through the JUNO-winning Balance, Bad Dreams and Monsters in the Closet era, making him one of the more recognizable voices in West Coast Canadian hip-hop.

Madchild's solo career became a major second chapter after addiction and personal instability interrupted the group's momentum. His first full-length solo album, Dope Sick, arrived in 2012 after months of writing during his recovery from an OxyContin addiction and turned that experience into unusually direct material about self-destruction, sobriety and rebuilding. He followed it with releases including Switched On, Silver Tongue Devil and The Darkest Hour, maintaining a prolific independent catalogue alongside later Swollen Members records and touring.

On 2019's Demons, Madchild returned explicitly to the subject of addictive behaviour and the ongoing work of recovery rather than presenting sobriety as a finished narrative. By the 2020s, his solo career and renewed work with Swollen Members had given him a rare degree of longevity within Canadian underground rap. His significance is tied both to the commercial breakthrough of his group and to the independent Battle Axe ecosystem that helped sustain a dedicated national audience outside mainstream radio cycles.
Toronto-born singer, songwriter, producer and multi-instrumentalist Maddee Ritter is a Canadian artist whose soulful alternative folk blends indie rock, R&B and jazz with intimate queer storytelling.

Maddie Bay is a France-born, Montréal-based singer-songwriter, vocalist and producer whose alternative pop-folk blends delicate acoustic writing with electronic textures. Her professional bio identifies Maddie Bay as her artist project and notes that she has been living in Canada for several years. Her 2026 single fin pm is her Northern Dial library credit.
Toronto producer and rapper Madlocks is a Canadian hip-hop artist whose late-1990s solo work followed years producing for acts including Ghetto Concept, Michie Mee and Diemen X.

Toronto rapper Maestro is an alternate credit for Maestro Fresh Wes, the pioneering Canadian MC whose platinum-selling debut and landmark single Let Your Backbone Slide helped establish hip-hop nationally.
Montréal singer-songwriter Magi Merlin makes gritty, groove-heavy alternative R&B, pairing sharp writing with soul, hip-hop and experimental-pop influences.

MAGIC! formed in Toronto around singer-songwriter and producer Nasri Atweh, guitarist Mark Pellizzer, bassist Ben Spivak and drummer Alex Tanas, combining pop songwriting with reggae and rock rhythms. Atweh was already an established hit writer before the group launched, and that studio experience gave MAGIC! an unusually polished debut. Their first album, Don't Kill the Magic, arrived in 2014 with "Rude," a breezy reggae-pop single that moved rapidly from Canadian radio to an international audience.

"Rude" reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in July 2014 and stayed there for six weeks, making MAGIC! the first Canadian band since Nickelback in 2002 to top the chart. The song also won the JUNO for Single of the Year and became one of the clearest examples of a Canadian band's ability to break globally during the streaming-era transition. Follow-up singles such as "Don't Kill the Magic" extended the group's visibility, while later albums Primary Colours and Expectations pushed the sound toward broader pop and R&B territory.

MAGIC!'s place in Canadian pop history rests primarily on the scale of that breakthrough, but the band's story is also about songwriting infrastructure. Atweh's career as a writer and producer connected the group to a wider international pop network, while the band's reggae-fusion approach placed it in a lineage of Canadian artists who have adapted Caribbean musical language for mainstream audiences. Even if "Rude" remains the defining hit, its six-week U.S. No. 1 run gives MAGIC! a notable position in the country's modern pop export story.
Montréal duo Majical Cloudz was a Canadian electronic art-pop project led by Devon Welsh and Matthew Otto, known for sparse arrangements and intensely direct songwriting.
Toronto R&B duo Majid Jordan, formed by singer Majid Al-Maskati and producer Jordan Ullman, blends atmospheric R&B with electronic production and emotionally direct songwriting.

Guyana-born reggae singer Donna Makeda built her recording career in Canada after migrating there and establishing herself in Toronto's reggae community. She began releasing music in the early 1990s and has remained active across Canadian reggae stages, recordings and cultural events for decades. Her catalogue includes the 1993 reggae cover "Real Love" and later releases spanning roots, culture and dancehall-informed reggae.

Northern Dial's Makeda credit comes from Ghetto Concept's 2007 single "Liv Rock (feat. Makeda)." Streaming catalogue data connects that feature to the same Makeda artist catalogue that contains "Real Love," while reggae discography data identifies the performer behind "Real Love" as Donna Makeda. That track-level chain distinguishes her from unrelated artists using the Makeda name.

Donna Makeda has performed extensively across Canada, including Toronto, Hamilton, Ottawa, Montreal and Calgary, while maintaining strong ties to Guyana and the wider Caribbean reggae circuit. Her long-running Canadian career places her within the country's reggae history as both a recording artist and community figure.

Manchi is a Toronto hip-hop artist associated with the early-2000s Ghetto Concept orbit. Northern Dial carries Manchi on Ghetto Concept's 2002 single 'Westend Story' alongside J-Wyze, Ray Smoove, Madlocks, DJ G-Starr and Black-I. Contemporary and retrospective Toronto hip-hop references place Manchi within the same local scene around Ghetto Concept and Infinite.

Manna Music is a Canadian producer, songwriter and creative director working at the intersection of Punjabi music, hip-hop and pop. After first building an audience through remixes and DJ work, he moved into music direction and production with artists including Karan Aujla, Deep Jandu, DIVINE and Inderpal Moga, while also founding Double M Records and earning Canadian industry recognition including a JUNO nomination.

Québec rapper and songwriter Manu Militari is a major voice in francophone Canadian hip-hop, known for detailed narrative writing, social observation and an independent career dating to the early 2000s.
